records.kind: government moves to postpone the bank's policy vote
records.summary: At the Monetary Policy Meeting of 11 August 2000 the delegates of the Ministry of Finance and the Economic Planning Agency filed a request under Article 19, Paragraph 2 of the Bank of Japan Law that the Policy Board postpone the vote on ending the zero interest rate policy, on the grounds that termination was premature; the Board put the request to a vote under Paragraph 3 and rejected it by eight votes to one, after which the government representatives expressed deep regret.
records.source_title: Bank of Japan, Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting on August 11, 2000 (with Attachment 2, 'On the Request from the Government to Postpone the Vote')
records.quote: the MOF and EPA representatives filed a request, pursuant to Article 19, Paragraph 2 of the Bank of Japan Law, that the Policy Board postpone ... a vote

records.summary: The federal government brought Bill C-114, 'an Act to declare the office of the Governor of the Bank of Canada to have become vacant', against Governor James Coyne; the Senate Standing Committee on Banking and Commerce reported on 13 July 1961 that the bill should not be further proceeded with and that the Governor had not misconducted himself in office, and Coyne resigned the same afternoon at 5.30 p.m.
records.source_title: Statement by J. E. Coyne, 13 July 1961 (Bank of Canada Open Archive Repository, record 2355)
records.quote: the charges brought against me by the Government in relation to Bill C-114, an Act to declare the office of the Governor ... to have become vacant

records.summary: On the evening of 17 October 2017 the Chamber of Deputies approved a motion tabled by Partito Democratico deputies which criticised Banca d'Italia's banking supervision and asked, indirectly but explicitly, that Governor Ignazio Visco's mandate not be renewed, saying his replacement should be the figure most suited to guaranteeing renewed confidence; Visco was nonetheless reappointed on 27 October 2017.
records.source_title: Il Post, 'Cosa sta succedendo tra PD e Banca d'Italia' (18 October 2017)
records.quote: la figura piu idonea a garantire nuova fiducia

records.summary: The House of Lords Economic Affairs Committee published 'Making an independent Bank of England work better' on 27 November 2023 after an inquiry into the Bank's operational independence, finding that the Bank's remit had grown in ways that risked jeopardising its ability to prioritise its primary objectives, recommending that the Treasury trim the remit and that Parliament review the Bank's remit and operations every five years.
records.source_title: Making an independent Bank of England work better, Economic Affairs Committee, 1st Report of Session 2023-24, HL Paper 10, ordered to be printed 17 November and published 27 November 2023 (House of Lords)
records.quote: The operational independence of the Bank of England should be preserved.

records.summary: Parliament called for written submissions on the South African Reserve Bank Amendment Bill, a private member's bill introduced by the Economic Freedom Fighters, which would make the state the Reserve Bank's sole shareholder in place of its private shareholders, provide for the government to appoint the board of directors and set appointed directors' tenure, and let the finance minister make regulations on those appointments and appoint the bank's auditors.
records.source_title: BusinessTech, 'EFF's plan to nationalise South Africa's Reserve Bank takes first step' (2 November 2020)

records.summary: The Oireachtas Joint Committee of Inquiry into the Banking Crisis examined the conduct of the Central Bank of Ireland and the Financial Regulator and found in its report that in the years 2000 to 2008 no enforcement action was taken against any institution for prudential breaches, that the Financial Regulator did not identify or escalate the systemic risk building in the banking sector, and that the Central Bank's own assessment of that build-up was weak.
records.source_title: Joint Committee of Inquiry into the Banking Crisis, Report Volume 1, 'Findings and recommendations'
records.quote: In the years 2000 - 2008, there was no enforcement action taken against any institution for prudential breaches.

records.summary: The February 2015 budget and the accompanying Finance Bill proposed stripping the Reserve Bank of India of its power to manage public debt and to regulate the government bond market, Finance Minister Arun Jaitley arguing the RBI faced a conflict of interest; on 30 April 2015 Jaitley asked the Speaker of the lower house to strike the provisions from the bill before debate began, a rollback reported as a victory for the RBI, which had opposed the changes.
records.source_title: Reuters via Business Standard, 'India puts financial overhaul on hold after RBI pushback' (30 April 2015)
records.quote: India shelved the overhaul ... Jaitley asked the lower house speaker to strike the provisions from the finance bill

records.summary: The Congress of Deputies' commission of inquiry into the financial crisis concluded that the supervisors, and the Banco de Espana above all, misjudged the situation and failed to stop the crisis, one approved conclusion holding that the Banco de Espana committed a grave irregularity with disastrous consequences by allowing Caja Madrid, Bancaja and five other savings banks to book a 7,619 million euro deterioration against reserves, and Congress agreed to send the report to the public prosecutor so that the role of the Banco de Espana and the CNMV could be investigated.
records.source_title: El Independiente, 'El Congreso pedira a la Fiscalia que investigue el papel del Banco de Espana y la CNMV' (28 February 2019)
records.quote: incurrio en una grave irregularidad de consecuencias nefastas

records.summary: Banco de Mexico's own official history records that generalised exchange controls and the expropriation of the private banks were prepared in secret between February and June 1982 and announced by President Jose Lopez Portillo despite the central bank's warnings, its director general Miguel Mancera having argued in an April 1982 pamphlet that controls were more than doubtful as a means of stopping capital flight, and that Lopez Portillo wanted Banco de Mexico turned into a decentralised public body and disliked its institutional style.
records.source_title: Banco de Mexico, Historia del Banco de Mexico, Tomo XVI: 'Las consecuencias del inflacionismo'
records.quote: exactamente los argumentos que habia desarrollado el director general del Banco de Mexico, Miguel Mancera, en su folleto de abril de ese ano

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Section 1-4 of Norway's Central Bank Act of 21 June 2019 provides that the King in Council may take decisions on the objectives of central banking activity, and that Norges Bank may be instructed in its activities in extraordinary situations, such a decision to be taken by the King in Council with the bank given an opportunity to be heard first and the Storting informed as soon as possible; section 1-10 lets the King in Council assign further tasks to the bank.
records.source_title: Lov 21. juni 2019 nr. 31 om Norges Bank og pengevesenet mv. (sentralbankloven), as published by Norges Bank
records.quote: Norges Bank kan ikke instrueres i sin virksomhet etter loven ... unntatt i ekstraordinaere situasjoner

blanks.verdict: vein closed (on the objection route only)
blanks.note: The 'law the bank objected to in writing' shape was tested for Germany and is closed: the Bundesbank's own Pressenotizen of 23 March 2001 (Stellungnahme des Zentralbankrats zur Reform der Bundesbankstruktur und der Finanzmarktaufsicht) and 22 March 2002 were both read in full, and in both the bank supports the federal finance ministry's restructuring of the Bundesbank Act rather than objecting to it. The 2002 statutory rewrite is filed above as a law change with that support stated plainly in the record, so a reader is not left thinking the bank resisted. I considered and rejected the September 2010 departure of Executive Board member Thilo Sarrazin: the application for his dismissal came from the Bundesbank's own board, so it is the bank acting on itself rather than a state organ acting on the bank, even though the Federal President is the dismissing organ.

REFUSED at round 70, and the reasoning settles a question this row had not faced squarely. The record offered was the Act amending the Bundesbank Act passed by the Bundesrat on 22 March 2002, which replaced the old governing structure with an eight-member Executive Board and ended the statutory reserved competences of the Direktorium and the Land central banks. That is a real restructuring of a central bank by the federal government -- and THE BANK SUPPORTED IT. The agent that found it also found the Zentralbankrat's Stellungnahme of 23 March 2001 backing the ministry's restructuring and the Bundesbank's own Pressenotiz of 22 March 2002 welcoming the change, and flagged the problem itself rather than filing quietly. THE RULE: this row records the state moving AGAINST the bank, and where the bank's own governing council consented in writing there is no adversary and nothing was done to it against its will. That is the converse of the caveat already written into the Nicaragua record, which says to reverse it if a round ever decides that a bank which GAINS power has not been moved against. A bank that consented has not been moved against either. Germany already holds a record on this row -- the 1997 plan to change the Bundesbank law and revalue its gold, which the bank's council called a possible attack on its independence -- so nothing is lost by refusing this one, and the contrast between the two is exactly the point: in 1997 the bank objected and in 2002 it agreed. The separate objection route was also closed this round: there is no German instance found of a law the Bundesbank opposed in writing beyond the 1997 episode already filed, and the September 2010 Sarrazin departure was considered and rejected because the dismissal application came from the Bundesbank's own board rather than from an organ of the state.
